name: moe_cache_thrashing_past_batch_480
description: fmoe bf16/fp8 kernel HBM BW degrades from 4.05 TB/s at batch=480 to 0.71 TB/s at batch=8613 on MI325X due to L2 thrashing; optimize the 480-1547 regime, not high-batch
preconditions: MI325X / MI300X with ~192 MB L2 shared across CUs
steps: Measure batch-to-BW curve before optimizing; confirm the drop-off shape matches the profiled table (67% at 480 -> 12% at 8613)
If working in the >=batch=2907 regime, do NOT blame kernel inefficiency: this is L2 thrashing, not a kernel defect
Direct optimization effort at batch 480-1547 (40-67% peak) where headroom exists
For high-batch uplift, attack the CACHE problem: persistent expert co-residency, weight compression past fp8, expert batching by router affinity -- not MFMA scheduling
expected_impact: avoids wasted optimization cycles on memory-wall-dominated high-batch regimes; redirects effort to the 480-1547 sweet spot
decision_rules: If achieved_BW < 1 TB/s at batch >= 2907, stop kernel-level optimization and attack L2 residency
